title: Hafele Dialock Compatible RFID Hotel Key Cards — Dual-Standard Chip Matrix
kicker: Hafele Dialock Compatibility by Lock Model
summary: ProudTek RFID cards are fully compatible with Hafele Dialock hotel locks across the DT 700/750 and LockerLock 300 models supporting both MIFARE ISO/IEC 14443A and Tag-it ISO/IEC 15693 standards. Hafele Dialock locks feature unique dual-standard architecture that supports MIFARE Classic EV1, MIFARE DESFire EV2 on the 13.56 MHz Type A band plus Tag-it HF-I on the 15693 Type B band for properties requiring longer read range and through-material reading capability. Hafele Dialock's German engineering makes it ideal for mixed hospitality and commercial access environments where hotel guest rooms, locker access, back-of-house areas and parking facilities must operate on unified credential infrastructure. Selecting the correct standard and chip family ensures compatibility across all door types and prevents reader timeouts that stall check-in workflows. The compatibility matrix on this page maps every current Dialock lock model to its supported standards, chip families and ProudTek card SKU verified through internal test-bench validation. Properties can leverage Hafele Dialock Software Suite integration to automate room-key encoding and multi-facility access workflows. Request a free test-card kit to verify on-site compatibility with your specific Dialock hardware before committing to a production order.

faq.question: What is the difference between Dialock Type A (MIFARE) and Type B (Tag-it) credentials?
faq.answer: Type A uses MIFARE (ISO/IEC 14443A) with 5-10cm read range, ideal for guest rooms and standard access doors. Type B uses Tag-it HF-I (ISO/IEC 15693) with 50-100cm read range, ideal for accessibility, convenience and through-material reading (safes, lockers). Hafele Dialock supports both standards simultaneously, allowing properties to optimize each access point.

faq.question: Can I use Tag-it HF-I cards for Dialock guest room locks?
faq.answer: Yes. Tag-it HF-I cards are fully compatible with Dialock DT 700 and DT 750 guest room locks and offer the benefit of longer contactless read range. However, Tag-it encoding is recommended only if your property values accessibility and guest convenience over the simpler MIFARE encoding workflows. For most guest-room applications, MIFARE Classic EV1 is the standard choice.

faq.question: Can I mix MIFARE and Tag-it credentials on the same Dialock estate?
faq.answer: Yes. This is a core advantage of Hafele Dialock's dual-standard platform. You can deploy MIFARE credentials for guest rooms, DESFire for back-of-house, and Tag-it for LockerLock 300 and accessibility zones — all managed by a single Dialock Software Suite instance without hardware changes.

faq.question: Which chip is best for Hafele Dialock LockerLock 300?
faq.answer: Tag-it HF-I is recommended for LockerLock 300 because its 50-100cm read range makes locker access more convenient and reduces wear on physical reader contact points. MIFARE Classic EV1 is also supported but requires closer credential proximity. ProudTek provides test cards of both to help you evaluate locker-access usability.

faq.question: How do I find my Dialock lock model and software version?
faq.answer: Lock model numbers (DT 700, DT 750, LockerLock 300) are printed on the lock housing or visible in the Dialock Software Suite Device Management interface. Software version can be found in the About or System Settings menu. Providing these details when requesting a test kit ensures ProudTek encodes sample cards against your exact configuration and standard support.

faq.question: What happens if I encode a Type B (Tag-it) card in a Type A (MIFARE) encoding profile?
faq.answer: The Dialock Software Suite will reject the card encoding because the credential format does not match the selected encoding profile. You must select the correct standard (Type A or Type B) before encoding each batch. ProudTek provides dual-standard encoding test scripts to help validate compatibility with your Dialock software configuration.

faq.question: Does ProudTek offer pre-encoded Hafele Dialock-compatible cards?
faq.answer: ProudTek ships cards with the correct chip, antenna and MIFARE or Tag-it configuration but does not pre-encode guest-room credentials. Room-key encoding must occur at the property through Dialock Software Suite because it requires real-time PMS data such as room number, check-in date and access level. ProudTek can pre-encode common-area access credentials if you provide the access-group configuration file.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for Dialock-compatible cards?
faq.answer: Plain white MIFARE Classic EV1 or Tag-it HF-I cards start at 300 pieces per order. Custom-printed cards with hotel branding require a 500-piece minimum to cover the offset printing setup cost. Test-card kits of 5 pieces are available free of charge for new compatibility verification projects. Volume pricing tiers start at 5,000 and 10,000 pieces with per-card cost reductions of 10-15%.

faq.question: Can Hafele Dialock-compatible cards include a magnetic stripe?
faq.answer: Yes. ProudTek produces dual-interface cards with both RFID (Type A or Type B) and ISO 7811 HiCo magnetic stripe. Some Dialock properties use the magstripe for legacy system access or elevator control while the RFID chip handles room locks and locker access. The combo card costs approximately 12-18% more than RFID-only cards at the 5,000-piece tier.
